The Transformer uses sinusoidal positional encodings [AIAYN:3.5:c020]. They may allow the model to extrapolate to sequence lengths longer than those seen during training [AIAYN:3.5:c020].
The ratio loss in H-Net is inspired by load balancing in Mixture-of-Experts models [HNET:2.2.3:c031]. It guides the network toward targeted compression ratios [HNET:2.2.3:c031].
Restricted self-attention would consider only a neighborhood of size r around each output position [AIAYN:4:c022]. This would increase the maximum path length to O(n/r) [AIAYN:4:c022].
Multi-head attention projects the queries, keys and values h times [AIAYN:3.2.2:c013]. It uses one shared projection for every head [AIAYN:3.2.2:c013].
The Transformer uses sinusoidal positional encodings, and these clearly outperformed learned positional embeddings [AIAYN:3.5:c020].
H-Net adds a projection only to the residual connection, because projections on the main path lowered perplexity in every experiment [HNET:2.3:c035].
A self-attention layer connects all positions with a constant number of sequential operations, while a recurrent layer requires O(log n) sequential operations [AIAYN:4:c022].
Padding tokens make up about 65% of the tokens in English conversational speech, and the text tokens of consecutive words usually overlap [MOSHI:3.4.4:c049].
The smoothing module applies an exponential moving average, which removes the need for a routing module [HNET:2.2.2:c025].
The Transformer achieves a new state of the art on WMT 2014 English-to-German, but its best model is outperformed by previously reported ensembles [AIAYN:7:c034].
